content.title: What To Know Before Sunday’s 48th South Side Irish Parade
content.text: Credibility: Original Reporting On the Ground Sources Cited Original Reporting This article contains new, firsthand information uncovered by its reporter(s). This includes directly interviewing sources and research/analysis of primary source documents. On the Ground Indicates that a Newsmaker/Newsmakers was/were physically present to report the article from some/all of the location(s) it concerns. Sources Cited As a news piece, this article cites verifiable, third-party sources which have all been thoroughly fact-checked and deemed credible by the Newsroom. South Side Irish Parade on March 17, 2024. Credit: Alex Wroblewski/Block Club Chicago BEVERLY — The 48th South Side Irish Parade will step off from 103rd and Western Avenue at noon Sunday. Held the Sunday before St. Patrick’s Day, the annual South Side parade was founded in Morgan Park in 1979 by neighbors George Hendry and Pat Coakley. It was inspired by the original Southtown Parade, which was held on 79th Street before moving Downtown in 1960. Its co-founders, along with their wives, Mary Hendry and Marianne Coakley, gathered a group of 17 children — the Wee Folks of Washtenaw and Talman — to march around the 10900 blocks of Washtenaw and Talman. In the years that followed, the parade grew, moving to a nearby park and eventually to Western Avenue, where it is still held. No matter the weather, more than 100 participants are scheduled to march in this year’s parade, including the Wee Folks of Washtenaw and Talman. The “Wee Folks of Washtenaw and Talman” walk in the 1997 South Side Irish Parade. Credit: Provided/South Side Irish Parade Committee What To Look For Leading the march will be this year’s grand marshal, the Tunnel to Towers Foundation, and the parade honoree, St. Christina Parish in Mount Greenwood. The grand marshal and parade honoree are chosen each year by the parade committee to highlight and honor two organizations making an impact on the community. The parade committee announced this year’s honorees during a special ceremony Feb. 4 at King-Lockhart Park in Beverly. Also among the floats will be the queen of the South Side Irish Parade. Each year, the committee names a new queen to represent the parade throughout the year. Born and raised in Mount Greenwood, Erin Larkin was selected as this year’s parade queen in February. Larkin will ride through the parade in a convertible, waving to the crowd over the mile-and-a-half-long route. An alumna of St. Christina Elementary School and Mother McAuley High School, Larkin works as a children’s therapist. Five pipe bands, led off by the Chicago Stockyard Kilty Band, are scheduled to participate in this year’s parade. Six local high school marching bands and the 484th Army band will also bring music to the parade. Where To Celebrate Floats will begin staging ahead of the parade 9 a.m. Sunday The parade steps off at noon following a ribbon-cutting at 11:45 a.m. at 103rd and Western Avenue. The parade is expected to last two hours. Last year’s parade brought out an estimated 77,000 people, so make sure to arrive early if you want a front-row spot along the route. Neighbors often host parties with family and friends on parade day. A number of area businesses will also be open for visitors. The west side of Western Avenue has multiple pubs along the route for those of age. Americanos, 11060 S. Western Ave., will open 11 a.m. Cork & Kerry, 10614 S. Western Ave., will open at 11 a.m. Horse Thief Hollow, 10426 S. Western Ave., will open at 11 a.m. Joey’s Red Hots, 11500 S. Western Ave., will open at 10:30 a.m. Nicky’s of Beverly, 10500 S. Western Ave., will open at 10 a.m. O’Kelly’s Bakery, 9100 S. Western Ave., will open at 8 a.m. Open Outcry Brewing, 10934 S. Western Ave., will open at 10 a.m. Fox’s Restaurant and Pub, 9956 S. Western Ave., will open at 11 a.m. Ken’s on Western, 10522 S. Western Ave., will open at 11 a.m. Mr. Submarine, 10509 S. Western Ave., will open at 9 a.m. South Side Irish Parade on March 17, 2024. Credit: Alex Wroblewski/Block Club Chicago Traveling Through The Neighborhood Expect travel restrictions on Sunday. Beginning at 6 a.m., no street parking is allowed on Western Avenue from 99th to 119th streets. Starting at 7 a.m., there will be no street parking allowed on the east side of Artesian Avenue from 103rd to 111th streets and on the west side of Claremont Avenue from 103rd to 107th streets. Starting at 9 a.m., traffic restrictions will be in place on all east/west streets leading to Western Avenue between 103rd and 115th streets. The traffic restrictions are expected to be lifted by 3 p.m. Parking will be limited throughout the area. Spectators are encouraged to walk on parade day. For those coming from out of the neighborhood, Metra is providing extra service on the Rock Island Line. Parade Committee Focused On A Safe, Family-Friendly Celebration The South Side Irish St. Patrick’s Day Parade Committee aims to ensure a safe, family-friendly celebration of Irish heritage and culture. The volunteer committee works with the city of Chicago, local community groups, schools and neighbors to present a family-friendly annual march down Western Avenue. Kids cry out for candy during the Chicago South Side Irish St. Patrick’s Day Parade on Sunday, March 16, 2025. Credit: Arturo Fernandez/For Block Club Chicago There will be security checkpoints surrounding the parade route, staffed by private security and police. Police will issue tickets for any drinking on the public way, including streets, sidewalks, alleys and areas close to the parade. Over 190 portable toilets will be along the parade route, with one at each street corner, according to the committee. The parade is operated by the South Side Irish St. Patrick’s Day Parade and Heritage Foundation, a nonprofit that works year-round to continue the family-friendly celebration. The parade committee consists of over 30 members handling everything from logistics, float entries, sanitation, and sponsorship to related events, public relations, marshals, bands and merchandising.
